newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Megaworld '96 net good but investors wary.
newsitem.headline: Megaworld '96 net good but investors wary.

text.p: The 1996 earnings of Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc turned out better than expected but cautiousness prevails over the sustainability of the company's high income stream in the future, analysts said.

Megaworld reported that its consolidated net income in 1996 reached 2.69 billion pesos ($102.28 million), which included extraordinary gains of 696.75 million pesos from the sale of its share in the initial public offering last year of its housing developer Empire East Land Holdings Inc.
That would put its recurring net income for 1996 at 2.0 billion pesos, double than the 1995 net income figure of 957.5 million pesos.
Its consolidated revenues rose 24 percent to 9.86 billion pesos in 1996 from 7.94 billion pesos in 1995.
"I'm sure the 2.0 billion pesos were above most analysts' expectations," said Colbert Nocum, an analyst of ING Barings Securities who projected the 1996 net at 1.8 billion pesos.
Nocum said Megaworld's 1997 net income could reach a higher net profit of 2.5 billion pesos this year.

Analysts, however, said investors were worried about Megaworld's long-term prospects due to a projected office glut in 1998 and the unsustainability of demand for high-income residential projects, which are the core businesses of the company.
"Even though it's (Megaworld) cheap, I'd still say it's a sell," said Ivy Cayayan, an analyst of Philippine Asia Equity Securities.

Instead, analysts advised a shift to Megaworld's 64 percent-owned housing unit Empire East because of the strong demand for its product lines by a growing middle-income class. Megaworld sources two-thirds of its income from Empire East.
"The general sentiment for Empire East is positive," Cayayan said.

"The company is focusing on supplying the needs of the young, urban professionals as well as the early nesters whose disposable income have increased in proportion to the country's growth," said Michelle Benedicto, property analyst of Asian Capital Equities.
Analysts forecast Empire East to churn out a net income of 1.9 to 1.97 billion pesos this year, within the company's projection of 1.94 billion pesos.
Empire East logged a net income of 1.57 billion pesos in 1996 from 558 million pesos in 1995. Its revenues soared by 127 percent to 5.86 billion in 1996 from 2.58 billion pesos in 1995.
Megaworld vice president Cirilo Manlangit said in a statement the company had projected a net income this year of 2.8 billion pesos, up from the recurring net income of 2.0 billion pesos last year.
"While we take an optimistic view of the real estate market in general, we continue to forecast the market behavior of each segment and formulate our strategies accordingly," he said.

"Our revenue mix is distributed across a wide range of products consisting of residential, office and commercial types catering to different market segments ranging from high to middle and low end," he added. Conversion $ = 26.30 pesos
